flashcard_questions.q: What does akhirah mean in Islam?
What is barzakh in Islamic belief?
flashcard_questions.a: A state of waiting between death and the Day of Judgement.

flashcard_questions.q: What happens to the soul during barzakh?
flashcard_questions.a: It stays in the grave and is questioned by angels about its faith.

flashcard_questions.q: What is purgatory in Christian belief?
flashcard_questions.a: A state where souls are purified of sin before they can enter heaven.

flashcard_questions.q: Why do many Protestant Christians reject purgatory?
flashcard_questions.a: Jesus does not mention it directly in the Bible.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the immortality of the soul?
flashcard_questions.a: The belief that the soul is eternal and lives on immediately after death.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the resurrection of the body?
flashcard_questions.a: The belief that the dead will be physically raised at the end of time.

flashcard_questions.q: Which words of Jesus suggest the afterlife begins straight away?
flashcard_questions.a: Today you will be with me in Paradise (Luke 23:43).
Paradise — a state of eternal peace and happiness.
Hell — eternal suffering for those who have rejected God.

flashcard_questions.q: What do Hindus and Sikhs believe happens after death?
flashcard_questions.a: Reincarnation — being reborn in a new body.

flashcard_questions.q: How does Buddhist teaching on rebirth differ from reincarnation?
flashcard_questions.a: Buddhists teach rebirth with no permanent soul that passes on.

flashcard_questions.q: Why do atheists and humanists reject belief in an afterlife?
flashcard_questions.a: Science can only prove the physical world, so there is no evidence for a soul.

flashcard_questions.q: Why might someone who rejects an afterlife value human life more highly?
flashcard_questions.a: They see it as the only life a person will ever have.

flashcard_questions.q: Why does belief in an afterlife reinforce the sanctity of life?
flashcard_questions.a: Life is given by God, so only God should decide when it ends.

notes: 15 cards: 6 term→definition (akhirah, barzakh, purgatory, Jannah, Jahannam, immortality of the soul), 3 tradition→position (Protestant on purgatory, Hindu/Sikh, Buddhist), 1 belief→source (Luke 23:43), 2 practice→meaning (barzakh questioning, bodily resurrection), 3 argument→view (non-religious, value of life). Kept definitions tighter than the sister Akhirah lesson to avoid a duplicate deck.
